methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $31M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
TerraDepth is a Series C-stage transportation company that has raised $31.1M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of eight private transportation frontier-tech companies, including later-stage peers such as Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in a sufficiently narrow peer set to support median valuation multiples.

The stage-progression method applies here, using the $31.1M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $52.9M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector—the three identified sector peers did not meet the minimum threshold of three datapoints after filtering for stage and valuation tier proximity. Reliance on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion given the sector-specific capital intensity and stage variation in the comp set.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to one applicable method, supports a valuation range of $45M (low) to $61M (high), with a median point of $53M. Key uncertainties include the validity of raised capital as a valuation proxy absent disclosed revenue or unit economics, the representativeness of the 1.7x multiplier for this particular stage transition, and the early-stage risk profile relative to later-stage transportation peers in the comp set.
